findings.text: follow-on: the fault-text half of the change has no recorded negative control — the sole mutation in negative-control.log reverts _decisions_retryable only, so this test's assertion on the decide_one warning text is never shown red, and the brief's requirement that each new test fail when its guard is reverted is demonstrated for the retry half alone; add a second mutation that reverts decide_one/decide_batch to outcome.fault and record its red log.

follow-on: the manifest's evidence_inputs states _transient_transport_errors reuses the transient HTTP classes the call layer already handled elsewhere, but base llm.py at 5e8ea3b8e contains no such set — the tuple is newly constructed here from httpx directly, so the reuse claim is unsupported and a reader would wrongly believe a canonical shared set already existed.

item_verdicts.done_when: The reviewed done_when names no added failures, a kept negative-control log and a landed fragment; gate-base.log and gate-after.log each end their summary at 1 failed with the same pre-existing id tests/discovery/test_judgment.py::test_judgment_imports_nothing_from_the_search_llm_package, so the added-failure count is zero and both arms ran to their summary and EXIT lines.
item_verdicts.goal: The reviewed goal is that a failed Jev decision call says what failed and is retried; imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py:301 logs outcome.fault_text and imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3342 makes _decisions_retryable decide a transport fault by its type, so the landed change does what the goal states.
item_verdicts.manifest: The reviewed manifest records status complete, both gate arms with their failure_ids, and the negative-control log, and its baseline_suite/after_suite blocks are readable, but its evidence_inputs claim that _transient_transport_errors reuses a set the call layer already handled is unsupported by base llm.py.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The brief grants four paths (judgment.py, llm.py, tests/discovery/test_decision_fault_retry.py, the landing fragment); git diff --stat 5e8ea3b8e 810a064e1 changes exactly those four and nothing else.

justifications.durability: tests/discovery/test_decision_fault_retry.py:124 and :182 assert independent call counts (calls["n"] == 2 and == 3) that redden when the retry classification is reverted, and :205 asserts a literal warning string, but negative-control.log covers only the retry half.

justifications.fit: imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:1220 follows the module's small-helper idiom and imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py:89 records the text on the existing CallOutcome NamedTuple rather than adding a parallel field; no added name violates the naming rules.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:1220 and :3342 name a bare fault and retry a transport fault by type, and imas_codex/discovery/base/judgment.py:168 and :301 read the description at both entry points.
justifications.reuse: the capability search over imas_codex for an existing fault-description or transient-error-tuple owner found none, so fault_text is the first owner of that capability and _decisions_retryable extends the shared _is_retryable at llm.py:3362 rather than forking it.
